context: Minimap navigator for a 50,000-point fractal random walk: a zoomable main line+area chart synchronized with a brushable minimap overview, using LTTB downsampling for performance.
first_impression: Technically sophisticated interactive chart with good downsampling, but the area fill combined with an auto-rescaling Y axis creates a truncated-baseline violation.
what_works: LTTB downsampling is a principled, shape-preserving algorithm that avoids introducing visual deception; scale domains are data-driven via `d3.extent` throughout, with no hardcoded magic numbers.
what_doesnt: Area fill closes to `mainH - margin.bottom` (the chart bottom) while the Y domain is set to `d3.extent(slice)` — the baseline represents min(visible data), not zero, so the shaded area falsely implies magnitude-from-zero encoding; Y scale recalculates from the visible slice on every zoom, causing the subset metamorphic relation to fail (remaining points shift positions when any point leaves view).
